raw_comment:
This graph shows the locations of droughts and their respective severities in the United States, which are represented by how saturated the shade of yellow is. Much of the eastern coast of the US does not have severe droughts, but is considered to be abnormally warm. The western coast, on the other hand, is a mix of abnormally dry, moderate, and severe. The areas with the most severe droughts are along the midwest and the south, with the states of Wyoming, Montana, S.D and N.D in the north, and New Mexico, Texas, and Oklahoma in the south. These states have the most numerous and severe droughts. 

What Do You Wonder - I wonder why most of the center of the United States faces the most severe droughts, and why the droughts in the extreme east and west boundaries are generally not as severe. Is it due to the proximity to the ocean? In addition, why are the droughts within the Ohio and West Virginia area so severe compared to the rest of the east coast?

Relation to Community - Though the conditions in New Jersey may not be as severe as in the midwest, there are still major implications for the communities surrounding it. Drier conditions will strain water resources, especially when the demand is higher during the summer months. Droughts can also affect air quality by increasing dust and particulates and harm ecosystems that depend on stable water supplies.

Headline - From Coastlines to Heartlands: Scorching Heat in the Heart of the US!
